chapter_title: Concerning the Man who is ugly in his Body, [but]
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation — The Formation of Wisdom's Goods in the Natural Mind

---

**¶9:** Precious goods of wisdom do not arise in every condition of the natural mind, nor are they formed throughout the whole of natural knowledge indiscriminately. Rather, in particular states and dispositions within the natural mind, goods of wisdom are formed in them [GAP-1] — that field of natural knowledge, in which the [GAP-2: precious interior truths] shall be brought forth [GAP-3] this [GAP-4] what the natural mind shall [GAP-5] — the ardor of its self-love blazes from above and descends [GAP-6: into the lower faculties] and it produces preliminary external truths, like the single influx of divine truth that flows [GAP-7] downward as heavenly influx [GAP-8] is the truth [GAP-9: descen]ding first [GAP-10] — a preliminary external vessel is formed and descends [GAP-11] the genuine interior truths [GAP-12] the truths.

---

**¶10:** This influx of divine truth shall [GAP-13: descend] into the genuine interior truths and [GAP-14] and those truths received the influx and were united with the [GAP-15] existing state. They did not descend into the lowest depths of the natural mind, but they [GAP-16] — the influx remained upon the external surface of the truths [GAP-17] to it. The preliminary external vessel and the containing natural form are constituted [GAP-18] from this wholesome influx of divine truth [GAP-19] it, and it becomes a good of [GAP-20: wisdom] — that which produces an influx of heavenly truth [GAP-21] truths [GAP-22] — it not being whole and undivided. It is dispersed and separated into many particular truths, and it requires a duration of state to become a unified genuine truth [GAP-23] and rises within the natural mind of [GAP-24] heavenly influx and genuine interior truth; and it is received into the containing form, which at first was merely a preliminary external vessel. They are conjoined with one another at [GAP-25: this] season of providential preparation, and are ordered and become a great good of wisdom — a great and precious kind.

---

**¶11:** When, however, an influx of heavenly truth descends, and that influx breaks into many particular truths and various fragments of perception, they shall be formed into and enclosed within numerous goods of wisdom, within the containing form and the external natural vessel. One vessel may form two goods of wisdom, another may form three, others may form five; some bring forth more than these, some fewer.

---

**¶12:** Now, when one might [GAP-26: receive a] complete and undivided influx of divine truth, and the containing form receives it whole, it shall become a great and precious good of [wis]dom, as its perfection is brought to fullness. [GAP-27: However], if two particular truths will have sufficient duration to adhere to one another before any fragment of truth escapes, and they unite with each other, and the containing form [GAP-28] before they disperse into [GAP-29] within [GAP-30] in a great and noble kind [GAP-31] — the influx of heavenly truth, which [GAP-32] another influx, that [GAP-33] the interior truths form them into [GAP-34: and] into a great and precious good.

---

**¶13:** Behold, [GAP-35: I have] taught you how goods of wisdom within the natural mind shall be formed. I have revealed to you that as a good of wisdom comes into existence by means of heavenly influx that has sufficient duration to become a preliminary external vessel, the containing natural form comes into existence by means of that preliminary vessel, and the preliminary vessel itself comes into being by means of the transformation and the [GAP-36: agitation] of the natural mind.

---

**¶14:** Then immediately at the season when [GAP-37] those who search the depths of the natural mind for spiritual goods recognize it, they shall [GAP-38] and they [GAP-39: descend] into those interior states and they bring goods of wisdom up from the depths of the natural mind, and each seeker finds according to the providence that is ordained for him. Those who retrieve these goods shall give them to those who communicate truths, and those who communicate truths deliver them to the governing loves of the celestial kingdom and to the ruling principles of good.

---

**¶17:** For all the interior affections that ascend while still within the corporeal state of the natural man and are liberated from it shall be restored to the great heavenly states of wisdom. A state of peace comes about for them, in that place within the states of celestial fullness.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: “Pearls shall arise not in every place in the sea, nor be formed in the sea as a whole. Rather, in various places that are in this sea, pearls are formed in them [ ... ... ] that sea, in which the [pearls] shall be formed [in] this [ ... ... ] what the sea shall [ ... ... ] its fire blazes above and comes [down to the depths of the sea] and it makes foam like the drop of water that flows [and comes] down in rainwater [which] is the water [that from above comes d]own first [and from it is formed] foam and comes down [and it comes to] the sweet waters [that are within] the waters.

“This drop of water shall [come] down to the sweet waters and [mingle] and they absorbed them and were combined with the [waters]. They did not [d]escend to the depths of the sea, but they [remained above, and] it floated on the surface of the waters [ ... ... ] to it. The foam and the pearl-shell shall be formed [from] this wholesome drop [that enters into] it, and it becomes a pe[arl. When] that makes a drop of rainwater [fall to the] waters [with] it not being whole. It breaks and separates out into many droplets, and it has time to become a drop of sweet water [again] and comes up in the sea of [the] rain and sweet water; and it is accomodated in the shell, which at first is foam. They shall be joined with each other at [this] time, and are shaped and become a great pea[r]l, a great and valued kind.

“When, however, a drop of rainwater falls, and that drop breaks into many droplets and various particles of water, they shall be formed into and be confined in [n]umerous pearls, in the shell and the pearl-shell. One might form two pearls, another may form three, others may form five; some mould more than these, some fewer.

“Now, when you might [find a] whole drop, and the shell receives it, it shall become a great and valued [pe]arl as its worth is perfected. [However], if these two droplets will have time (to adhere) to one another before any (water particle} escapes, and they mix with e[ach o]ther, and the shell [receives them] before they break into [many] within [it] in a great kind [ ... ... ] the drop of rain, which [has time to adhere to] another one, that [ ... ... ] the [w]aters form them in [it and] in a great, valued commodity.

“Behold, [I, I have] taught you how sea-pearls shall be formed. I have told you that as a pearl shall come into existence by means of rainwater that has [ti]me to become foam, the pearl-shell shall come into existence by means of the foam, and the foam itself comes into being by means of the transformation and the [agitation] of the sea.

“Then immediately at the time when [the rain falls upon the sea] the pearl divers know it, they shall [come] and they [go d]own to those places and they bring pearls up from the depths of the sea, and each pearl diver finds according to the fortune that is [ordai]ned for him. The pearl divers shall [gi]ve them to the traders, and the traders give them to the kings and the nobles.

“Fo[r a]ll the souls that ascend in the flesh of mankind and are freed shall be brought back to the great aeons of light. A place of rest comes about for them, at that place in the aeons of greatness.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading identifies these as "precious interior truths," which in the natural-plane vocabulary of this chapter corresponds directly to "pearls" — the central subject of the teaching.

The preposition "in" connects "shall be formed" to "this [sea/place]," indicating the location where pearls are brought forth, matching the spiritual sense of being formed within a specific field of natural knowledge.

fills.fill: down to the depths of the sea
fills.explanation: The sea's fire blazes above and descends into the sea's depths, corresponding to the spiritual sense of self-love's ardor penetrating into the lower faculties, producing the disturbance that generates foam (preliminary external truths).
Double-verb constructions ("flows and comes down") are characteristic of Coptic Kephalaia style, describing the descent of rainwater as divine influx flowing downward.

The relative pronoun "which" connects the preceding "rainwater" to "is the water," identifying the rainwater as the first water to descend — matching the spiritual sense that heavenly influx is the primary truth that descends.

Rainwater is identified as "the water that from above comes down first" — descending from above (heaven) before the foam, directly paralleling the spiritual sense of divine truth descending first, and echoing "blazes above" earlier in the same passage; "from above" (ⲉⲃⲟⲗ ϩⲛ ⲧⲡⲉ) is standard Coptic Kephalaia vocabulary.

The spiritual reading states "a preliminary external vessel is formed" — in natural terms, foam is formed from the descending rainwater; the rain comes down first and from it the foam (preliminary vessel) is produced, which then descends toward the sweet waters.

Coptic characteristically doubles motion verbs — "comes down and it comes to" mirrors the earlier "flows and comes down" — rendering what would be a ⲉⲓ ⲉⲡⲉⲥⲏⲧ ⲁⲩⲱ ⲁϥⲉⲓ ⲉ- construction, describing the foam's descent reaching the sweet waters within the sea.

The sweet waters are a distinct subset found within the broader waters of the sea, corresponding precisely to the spiritual sense of "genuine interior truths within the truths" — the preposition "within" captures the interior relationship that defines sweet waters as distinguished from the sea's general waters.
The spiritual reading says "descend," which in the Kephalaia's natural register with "down" following becomes "come down" — the standard motion verb for descent in this text's idiom.
The drop descends to the sweet waters and mingles with them before being absorbed, corresponding to the spiritual sense of divine influx being received by and united with genuine interior truths.
The drop and sweet waters were "combined with the waters" — the existing body of water/truth already present, matching the spiritual sense of being united with the existing state of truths.

The spiritual reading says "the influx remained upon the external surface" — in the natural register, the combined drops and sweet waters did not descend to the depths but remained above, creating a direct contrast with "the depths of the sea" in the preceding clause.

The preposition "from" indicates the origin/source: the foam and pearl-shell are formed FROM this wholesome drop, corresponding to the spiritual sense that the containing form is constituted from the wholesome influx of divine truth.

The wholesome drop enters into the forming foam and shell, becoming enclosed within it and transforming into a pearl — corresponding to the divine influx being received into the containing natural form and becoming a good of wisdom.

Completing "pearl" and introducing a temporal-conditional clause: "When that [which] makes a drop of rainwater fall to the waters, with it not being whole, it breaks..." — the spiritual reading's dash marks the transition to this conditional scenario describing what happens when the influx is not unified.

Rainwater naturally falls to the waters below, and the spiritual reading confirms the influx goes into the truths — "fall to the" is the standard Kephalaia motion describing descent of rain toward the sea's waters.

The preposition "with" introduces the attendant circumstance: "with it not being whole," describing the condition of the raindrop (divine influx) as it arrives — not unified, leading to its dispersal.

The droplets have time to become sweet water "again" — the scattered fragments of influx reform into genuine interior truth once more, before rising within the natural mind to be received by the containing form.
The definite article "the" specifies the previously described rain: "comes up in the sea of the rain and sweet water," identifying the particular rain (heavenly influx) already discussed.
The editor's "this" is confirmed; the spiritual reading identifies "this time" as the season of providential preparation when the scattered truths are conjoined into a unified good of wisdom.

The editor's "find a" is confirmed; while the spiritual reading uses "receive," the natural-plane register appropriately uses "find" for the observer's perspective, and avoids repetition with "the shell receives it" immediately following.

The editor's "However" is confirmed; it introduces the contrasting condition where two droplets adhere before separating, corresponding to the spiritual teaching about particular truths uniting before fragmenting.
The shell (containing natural form) receives the combined droplets before they can break apart, corresponding to the spiritual sense of the natural form containing the truths before they disperse.
Parallel to the earlier passage ("separates out into many droplets"), the shell receives them before they break into many — before the influx disperses into many particular truths.
The pronoun "it" refers back to the shell: the droplets remain within it (the containing form) in a great kind, rather than dispersing.

This directly echoes the key phrase from earlier in ¶12 — "these two droplets will have time (to adhere) to one another" — now restated as the drop of rain "which has time to adhere to another one," describing the same process of drops combining to form a great pearl.

The waters form the drops within the shell ("in it") and into a great valued commodity — a parallel construction where "it" refers to the containing form, corresponding to the spiritual sense of interior truths forming goods within the natural vessel.
The editor's "I, I have" is confirmed; the doubled first-person pronoun is a standard Coptic emphatic construction in Mani's direct speech throughout the Kephalaia.

The foam comes into being through the transformation and agitation of the sea — the sea's fire causes disturbance that produces foam, corresponding to the spiritual sense of the natural mind's perturbation producing preliminary external truths.

fills.fill: the rain falls upon the sea
fills.explanation: The entire chapter teaches that pearls form when rain descends into the sea; the pearl divers recognize this event as the trigger, corresponding to spiritual seekers recognizing when divine influx has entered the natural mind.

The pearl divers shall come (gather at the sea) and then go down to the places where pearls are found, corresponding to those who seek spiritual goods first assembling before descending into the depths of the natural mind.

Completing "go d" + "own" = "go down": the pearl divers go down to those places, corresponding to the spiritual sense of descending into interior states of the natural mind to retrieve goods of wisdom.
